papers.summary: Spectral weight decay applies additive singular-value shrinkage. In LLaMA models up to 500M parameters, the authors report lower effective rank and better SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss.
papers.relevance: Directly tests whether training can improve low-rank compressibility while preserving quality.

evidence.quote: For the 500 500 M model and a 4 % 4\% distortion budget, it supports 1.89 × 1.89\times compression, compared with 1.14 × 1.14\times after standard weight decay.

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: Ori tracks drifting gradient subspaces for low-rank LLM pretraining. Its reported advantage over GaLore is largest at stringent rank constraints, with optimizer-step memory and timing measured separately from total training memory.
papers.relevance: A direct comparison for memory-efficient pretraining under tight rank budgets.

evidence.quote: when training the 130M model at an aggressively low rank of just 16, Ori achieves a validation perplexity of 43.61, substantially outperforming GaLore (60.29) and OSD (54.05).
Our goal is to record the peak memory usage, incurred solely by the said optimizer’s update step.

papers.title: Ori: Drift-Aware Streaming $k$-PCA for Very Low-Rank LLM Training

papers.summary: Monarch–Muon combines structured weights with matrix-aware optimization. Quality runs compare 257M dense and 1B MoE models, while larger-width systems measurements separately assess memory and speed.
papers.relevance: Clarifies how model quality, training memory, and optimizer cost trade off with scale.

evidence.quote: Quality runs train a 257M dense reference and a 1B MoE reference on FineWeb-Edu ( Penedo et al., 2024 ) . Systems benchmarks cover dense reference sizes up to 6.89B on an H100.
From the 834M reference onward, Monarch–Muon improves both full-step time and peak memory relative to dense Muon.

papers.title: Monarch-Muon: Structure-Aware Muon for Fast and Memory-Efficient Pretraining

papers.summary: A module-matched LoRA rank sweep under label noise finds a second descent, but parameter-saving post-peak ranks remain worse than dense fine-tuning in the measured settings. The 7B experiment uses paired seeds and identical adapted modules.
papers.relevance: Direct evidence on rank, memorization, and generalization under noisy labels.

evidence.quote: Across four vision backbones and a 7 7 B language model, no measured post-peak rank that still saves parameters reaches dense
Seeds control the subset, the noise draw, the head init and the adapter init, and are shared across arms, so the differences below are paired.

papers.title: LoRA's Second Descent Extends Beyond Parameter Parity

papers.summary: An SVD-free Rényi-2 penalty encourages fuller use of LoRA adapter rank. In mixed-domain sweeps, it lowers mean Wiki perplexity relative to unpenalized LoRA at the stated ranks, though the learning–forgetting tradeoff remains configuration-dependent.
papers.relevance: Connects effective-rank regularization to practical language-model fine-tuning.

evidence.quote: In mixed-domain rank sweeps on three models, λ = 0.01 \lambda=0.01 lowers mean Wiki perplexity at every tested rank of at least 16 16 relative to unpenalized LoRA
the penalty can improve retention without a large training-fit cost, but does not eliminate the learning–forgetting trade-off.

papers.title: Maximizing Capacity Utilization of LoRA Adapters for Mitigating the Learning-Forgetting Trade-off

papers.summary: Analyzes singular-mode birth, saturation, and decay for several optimizer geometries in deep matrix factorization. Its phase laws depend on balance and alignment assumptions rather than establishing corresponding LLM-training effects.
papers.relevance: A theoretical framework for how optimization changes spectra and low-rank bias.

evidence.quote: Under explicit balance and alignment assumptions, we derive birth, saturation, and decay laws for Euclidean GD, coordinate-wise updates of SignGD and an instantaneous Adam approximation, spectral updates of Muon and cumulative Shampoo, and a block curvature model of K-FAC.
Although the phase laws rely on balance and alignment assumptions, they identify concrete mechanisms to understand optimizer behavior.

papers.title: Optimizer Geometry Sets the Pace: Spectral Learning Dynamics in Matrix Factorization

papers.summary: BMuon changes Muon's geometry to allocate a shared budget across MLP channels. In a 1B LLaMA-style experiment, it better withstands channel pruning but has worse unpruned perplexity than Muon.
papers.relevance: An important counterpoint: greater compressibility need not preserve uncompressed quality.

evidence.quote: On the unpruned models, Muon achieves lower perplexity ( 10.92 10.92 versus 12.84 12.84 for BMuon), but its performance degrades rapidly under pruning.
Overall, BMuon trades some unpruned quality for substantially greater robustness to structured channel pruning.

papers.title: BMuon: Budgeting Muon's Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility

papers.summary: CORE is a training-free deep-research harness that retrieves broad passages, returns selected snippets, and manages previously retrieved context. Controlled closed-search comparisons report higher answer accuracy and evidence recall across the tested model–benchmark combinations.
papers.relevance: Directly informs retrieval and context-management choices for a handwritten research-digest harness.

evidence.quote: CORE searches at the passage level but returns evidence at the snippet level.
Across three agent models, CORE achieves the highest accuracy and evidence recall in every model–benchmark comparison

papers.title: CORE: Coarse-to-Fine Search with Context Management for Deep Research

papers.summary: Defines LoRA compression by serialized adapter size required to retain held-out behavioral gain, rather than by rank or reconstruction error. Measured rates vary with the frozen base model; the rate is codec-dependent.
papers.relevance: Challenges numerical measures of adapter compressibility with a behavior-preserving criterion.

evidence.quote: the same datasets can require substantially different rates across frozen models, with their ordering changing across receivers.
R ⋆ R^{\star} is an operational, codec-dependent rate rather than an information-theoretic optimum

papers.title: The Behavioral Rate of Fine-Tuning: Compression as a Measure of Useful Information

papers.summary: Compares fine-tuning update rank measures against shape-matched random matrices, pretrained weights, and non-alignment fine-tunes. Updates can look nearly full rank by direction count yet spectrally concentrated by stable rank; some released updates are affected by BF16 rounding.
papers.relevance: Provides essential controls for interpreting effective rank and spectral concentration.

evidence.quote: The threshold count reads 91–99%, close to noise; stable rank puts every update 1.6 to 27 times below noise
A Gaussian matrix is the least structured baseline possible, and even the difference of two unrelated trained checkpoints beats it.

papers.title: Rank Measures of Fine-Tuning Updates Need a Noise Baseline
